tasks.goal: Find an approachable Vantage matchup from the lobby guide as a Gateway graduate
actionsEvidence: Clicked lobby Pairing & learning guide link; first recommendations name Vic central pressure vs Built to Last defensive economy and say learn tag management with complete familiar rig.
Switched pool to Vantage and selected exact recommended Vic and Built to Last deck names in lobby.
Guide separates AI-only results and preliminary samples and says custom decks unbenchmarked.
tasks.guideHelp: Three learning goals are an effective on-ramp; clear caveats prevent treating the 48% AI result as a human difficulty score.
tasks.externalKnowledge: Chose Vic partly because reviewer assignment requested coverage; no outside matchup information.
tasks.friction: Recommendation cards have no select/launch or deck-detail links. Need manual pool switch and name matching. Lobby includes both Vic central pressure and Vic Central pressure variants; exactness matters.
tasks.improvement: Add a Try this pairing button to each recommendation, preselecting exact pool and both deck IDs. Add Read the deck plan with two first-turn priorities and important new cards.
tasks.howToTest: Fresh Gateway-profile session: ask a Gateway graduate to launch recommended Vic pairing; confirm exact vic-play-v1 and weyland-vantage-tools-v2 selected without name hunting or accidental pilot selection.

tasks.goal: Use guide alone to choose one small legal Runner edit

actionsEvidence: Entire rendered guide contains pairing/results instructions but no cuts/adds, sample edit, or deckbuilding legality explanation.

Changed -1 Marjanah +1 Docklands Pass; builder says Changes +1 Docklands Pass -1 Marjanah, 45 cards, 13/15 influence, Ready to play.
tasks.guideHelp: The central-pressure learning goal provides broad intent, and custom-deck warning correctly removes benchmark certainty after edits.
tasks.externalKnowledge: Reviewer supplied the idea that an extra Docklands Pass supports HQ multiaccess and that reducing redundant Marjanah while retaining two Cleavers/two Marjanahs preserves barrier coverage. The guide does not teach this reasoning or the copy limit. Builder supplies legality feedback; own Netrunner knowledge supplies card-role and redundancy judgments.
tasks.friction: Guide-only task cannot be completed. What to learn next is not an actionable deckbuilding exercise. No link to Tune deck or a worked edit/tradeoff.
tasks.severity: medium; missing educational scope, not a claim the pairing page promises a full deckbuilding tutorial
tasks.improvement: Add one optional worked one-for-one exercise per recommended deck with card text links, role of the cut/add, before/after size/influence, and a question to observe in the next game. Link directly to editor with exact base deck and clearly label altered lists unbenchmarked.
tasks.howToTest: Give fresh Gateway graduates only the guide. Ask them to propose one legal edit and explain what function they are sacrificing; verify they can identify both cards, preserve complete breaker coverage and explain legality without outside rules.

tasks.guideHelp: Pairing was a useful starting point and Vic's goal prompted tag removal. The guide offered no turn plan, damage-budgeting example, economy recovery guidance, or postgame tuning question.
tasks.externalKnowledge: Substantial tactical Netrunner knowledge: public advanced remote urgency, damage buffer, breaking only relevant subs, economy reservation, targeted tutor, and deciding when server costs exceed budget. Exact choices were supplied by game UI card/subroutine details, not guide.
tasks.friction: No handoff from guide to play or postgame reflection. Save/reopen flow itself worked and clearly showed legal totals. Dynamic action panels sometimes changed between single-card and multi-card selection; routine scripting had harmless locator/timing misses, not evidence of human UI defects.
tasks.severity: medium for educational handoff; low/no observed save defect
tasks.improvement: Add short pregame checklist for this pair: establish income, find killer before revealed damaging sentries, count grip before accepting damage, check every advanced remote, use Vic after a tag. Add postgame prompts separating bad draws, tactical errors and deck edits; link back to exact saved deck.
tasks.howToTest: Observe a novice playing this pair with the checklist. Record whether they notice a 2+ advanced remote, inspect damage subs, retain a survival buffer, and use Vic once tagged. Ask for one evidence-based edit after game without claiming that one result proves strength.

game.editImpact: Extra Docklands Pass was drawn but never installed; this game does not show edit benefit or establish balance.

limitations: Single AI-driven usability session; reviewer already knows Netrunner and is simulating a Gateway graduate, so not a substitute for human novice testing.
No screenshot/visual certification due snapshot timeout and shared browser viewport changes.
Shared incognito storage contained other work; no storage clearing, global preference changes, deletion of others' decks or restoration performed. Parent restores environment.

Early setup/keep-hand clicks precede detailed automatic trace; setup notes and first-impression artifact preserve their sequence. Trace records successful named DOM clicks; failed locator/timing attempts are visible in tool transcript and had no game action.

Strategy confounds: early killer absence, optional Spin Doctor trash cost, expensive full-break remote steal and insufficient economy recovery created avoidable pressure. Winning last run used careful but risky damage arithmetic; it is not evidence that guide teaches beginner tactics.
Only session/config/final fields read after terminal; no private engine cards or direct action APIs used. No headless browser.
